summary: Ephemeral GCP deployer certificate mismatch prevents canary rollout in us-west/us-east
description: Issue summary: During the staged canary rollout for service 'inference-proxy' at 2026-03-12 18:05 UTC, the CI/CD pipeline failed when attempting to provision ephemeral GCP deployer certificates for new runners. Impact: Canary deployment halted in us-west and us-east, preventing automated promotion and blocking the release window. Environment: prod clusters in us-west / us-east; release triggered by release-engineering pipeline 'release/inference-proxy/v2.9.1'.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Trigger release/inference-proxy/v2.9.1 pipeline from release-engineering branch
2) Pipeline attempts ephemeral deployer cert issuance via infra-service account 'ci-deployer@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com'
3) Runner bootstrapping step 'bootstrap-deployer-creds' fails with certificate validation error and TLS handshake abort
4) Canary traffic not shifted, pipeline aborts due to failed smoke tests and healthchecks
observed_errors_and_logs: [2026-03-12T18:05:11Z] bootstrap-deployer-creds: ERROR: failed to fetch ephemeral cert: x509: certificate signed by unknown authority (issuer mismatch)
[2026-03-12T18:05:12Z] runner-init: WARN: falling back to cached kubeconfig (age=36h) - not allowed for ephemeral flows
GCP IAM audit: token issue event 7e3b2c in us-west showing 'audience mismatch' for signed JWT
impact: Canary rollout stalled in two regions. Manual promotion blocked. Estimated number of affected release windows: 1 (today). No customer-facing downtime, but release backlog now delayed and manual action required for every future ephemeral deploy until root cause fixed.
initial_triage_notes: Support received alert from release-engineering at 18:12 UTC via #release-engineering channel.
Checked recent secret-rotation job run: 'ephemeral-deployer-cert-rotation' completed at 2026-03-12T17:58 UTC; rotation logs show issuer change from 'ci-issuer-v3' to 'ci-issuer-v4'.
Hypothesis: cert rotation produced new issuer value but some regional caches or long-lived runners still expect old issuer; token audience validation failing during ephemeral cert exchange.
investigation_notes: 18:20 UTC - ran 'gcloud iam service-accounts keys list' and compared thumbprints between us-west and us-east; observed different metadata timestamps but same key id.

18:27 UTC - inspected infra service 'ephemeral-issuer' deploy: found rollout of issuer v4 started at 17:58 UTC; rollout completed in control plane but edge caches (runner bootstrapper CDN) still serving v3 metadata in us-west - cache TTL misconfiguration discovered.
18:35 UTC - reproduced failure locally by forcing bootstrap flow to use issuer v3 while CA bundle contained v4 root -> x509 issuer mismatch matches production logs.

18:42 UTC - confirmed pipeline step uses library 'runner-bootstrapping'@commit a1b3f4d which validates token 'aud' against canonical issuer value embedded in the artifact. The artifact was built before rotation and still has old issuer baked in.

18:50 UTC - Slack thread #release-engineering linked to #infra-openssl: noted that rotation job replaced CA content in secret 'ephemeral-deployer-ca' but did not trigger rebuild of ephemeral runner bootstrap image.
actions_taken: Rolled back rotation audit marker to allow legacy issuer v3 to be accepted by the cert exchange (temporary safeguard) at 19:05 UTC.
Issued manual requeue of canary pipeline at 19:12 UTC using a patched bootstrap image (runner-bootstrapping@a1b3f4e) that accepts both v3 and v4 issuers.
Validated canary succeeded in us-east at 19:28 UTC and us-west at 19:33 UTC; smoke tests passed and promotion proceeded to scheduled canary traffic percentages.
Created short-term gating: rotation job now pauses automatic image rebuilds until CI verifies compatibility across regional caches.
resolution: Workaround applied: patched bootstrap image (runner-bootstrapping@a1b3f4e) and temporary accept-list for v3 issuer allowed immediate canary resumption.

Root cause: CA rotation completed but did not trigger coordinated artifact rebuilds and CDN/cache invalidation in the runner bootstrap path; a timing gap between rotation and artifact refresh caused issuer mismatch in bootstrapping flows.

Permanent fix: implement coordinated rotation orchestration - rotation job will now perform three steps atomically: (1) update CA and secret, (2) trigger artifact rebuild of runner-bootstrapping, (3) invalidate bootstrapper CDN caches and wait for global propagation. New orchestration playbook committed to infra repo. See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/2387.
Postmortem owner: Diego Martinez. Postmortem to be published by 2026-03-16 and tied to confluence page 'runner-ephemeral-rotation-postmortem'.
Follow-ups: schedule an emergency test of rotation orchestration in a staging multi-region cluster (task INT-19012 created).
